title: Kestrel AI implementation orientation & runbook review
summary: Initial implementation orientation for Kestrel AI's pilot with Redwood Dedicated. Reviewed runbook, deployment options (VPC vs on-prem), SSO/SAML and KMS requirements, and proposed benchmark plan. Agreed next steps: share hardened runbook, schedule infra dry-run, and provide dedicated pricing template.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (p50/p95 latency, throughput)
next_steps: Redwood to send hardened runbook + playbook links
Schedule infra dry-run (SE + Kestrel infra) for 12/19
Priya to run preliminary perf benchmark on sample payloads and share spreadsheet
Redwood AE to share Dedicated pricing template and contract timeline
action_items: Priya Shah - run perf benchmarks and upload results to shared spreadsheet (due: 2025-12-16)
Jordan Blake - send hardened runbook and pricing template (due: 2025-12-13)
Tom Rivera - provide network diagram and firewall rules for VPC peering (due: 2025-12-15)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-12
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Li (Head of ML, Kestrel), Tom Rivera (Platform), Lisa Cho (Security), Amit Patel (CTO)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan from Redwood here, I'm the AE on the account, real quick agenda — orientation on the implementation runbook, answer any security questions, and plan the infra dry-run.
00:14 Maya: Thanks Jordan, excited to get started. We have a pilot so want to make sure the handoff is clean.
00:21 Jordan: Yep, and Priya'll talk through the runbook. Priya over to you.
00:26 Priya: Thanks. Hi team. I'll run through the runbook high level — pre-launch checklist, network, auth, model selection, perf benchmarks, and canary plan. Note: I might say KV cache funny or say K-V cash, I'm sorry.
00:45 Tom: (laughs) we've all done it.
00:48 Priya: First, infra options — you told us you prefer Dedicated in a VPC with peering to your account for isolation. That matches our Dedicated offering which can be VPC peered, or we can do a Private on-prem package if you need air-gapped. Which are we leaning to?
01:10 Maya: Dedicated VPC peering is what we want to try for pilot. We want the ability to fall back to hosted for burst.
01:18 Priya: Right, we recommend a hybrid routing policy — primary to Dedicated, fallback to Redwood-hosted instances for overflow. It keeps latency SLOs but preserves availability.
01:32 Lisa: Quick security note — we need SAML SSO tied to Okta, KMS integration for key management, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Are those supported out-of-box?
01:43 Priya: Yes. SAML/SSO via SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. KMS integrations are supported; we can either do customer-managed keys through AWS KMS or an HSM integration. Audit logs are exportable to your S3 or to our log ingestion endpoint. I'll add the exact retention config to the runbook.
02:05 Lisa: Great. Also need data residency note — some of our customers are EU and want data kept in eu-west-1. Can you pin region?
02:13 Jordan: We can pin region for Dedicated and Private. For hosted there are region preferences but not strict isolation unless you sign region-specific contracts.
02:23 Amit: On compliance, is Redwood SOC 2 Type II? We need the cert for procurement.
02:29 Jordan: Yes, SOC 2 Type II. We also have ISO docs; I'll upload to the shared drive.
02:35 Maya: Cool. Back to runbook — what's the typical cadence for kernel selection and quantization? We're running smaller GPUs and want to leverage 4-bit quantization for cost.
02:47 Priya: Our runtime supports quantized model variants; we can recommend Q4 or Q8 profiles per workload. In the runbook there's a model selection matrix — bias/quality tradeoffs vs perf. We'll propose quantization only after QA on prompt sets.
03:02 Tom: For the dry-run, which sample payloads should we use? We have multi-turn chat and a separate embedding pipeline for semantic search.
03:11 Priya: We'll ask for a small representative prompt set — ~200 multi-turn conversations and ~10k short texts for embeddings. That should give us p50/p95 latency and throughput numbers. We'll run continuous batching profiles to model real traffic.
03:27 Maya: Can you estimate cost differences between Dedicated and hosted for our projected 1M tokens/day?
03:34 Jordan: I'll send a dedicated pricing template after the call. Roughly, Dedicated will be more predictable per-month but lower per-token at scale with committed capacity. Hosted is pay-as-you-go but can spike costs. We'll include numbers in the template.
03:50 Lisa: Another security ask — can we restrict model access by RBAC within our team and tie to Okta groups?
03:58 Priya: Yes, RBAC maps to SAML groups and tokens are scoped. We'll detail token-level granularity and token rotation cadence.
04:12 (small cross-talk)
04:18 Jordan: Turning to the runbook doc — Priya, can you walk through the pre-launch checklist items?
04:23 Priya: Sure. Pre-launch checklist items: network & peering validated, KMS keys provisioned, SSO configured, service accounts created, model pinning and canary route defined, monitoring & alerting set up (latency, error rate, token spend), and security review completed. Also define rollback policy — automatic fallback to hosted variant after X minutes of degradation.
04:47 Tom: On firewall rules, what outbound ports do we need for peering? Do we need special NAT?
04:52 Priya: It's standard — allow egress to Redwood subnets over the peering connection; ports 443 for control plane and 8443 for internal runtime telemetry. We'll send a network diagram.
05:06 Tom: Ok, that's helpful.
05:09 Maya: There's a procurement timeline: legal needs SLA and logs retention terms. Jordan, can legal get the Dedicated contract draft?
05:18 Jordan: Yep, I'll share the template. We usually have a 30–45 day turnaround for small edits, faster if we have a consolidated list.
05:26 Lisa: Can we get a specific section called 'data deletion' and 'audit trail' in the contract? It's mandatory for our vendors.
05:33 Jordan: Absolutely. We'll include data deletion SLA (on request) and audit log retention options.
05:39 Priya: For the performance benchmark plan, we propose three runs: cold-start p95 without cache, warmed up runs with KV cache enabled, and embedding throughput runs with batch sizes tuned. We'll attach the spreadsheet with expected metrics.
05:58 Maya: What's the typical p95 for multi-turn with our model family? We're looking for <200ms ideally but willing to accept 300ms for complex prompts.
06:09 Priya: On Dedicated with optimized kernels and sequence lengths typical to your prompts, p95 often lands in the 120–250ms range for gpt-like models at batch size 1–4, depends on model size. We'll produce a real number in the benchmark.
06:26 Amit: One worry — we have a third-party legacy datastore that will issue high latency calls in some cases. Can we set timeouts so inference doesn't block downstream?
06:36 Priya: Yes, the runtime supports request timeouts and circuit breakers. We can also set per-route throttles and fallback responses.
06:46 Tom: About canary rollout — what percentage do you recommend for canary and how long?
06:50 Priya: Standard is 5–10% traffic for 24–72 hours depending on metrics. We'll instrument canary breakpoints by p95 latency and error rate. If breach, auto rollback to baseline.
07:06 Maya: For the onboarding playbook, will Redwood provide runbooks for incident response?
07:12 Priya: Yes — runbook includes incident types, run rates, who to page at Redwood, escalation matrix and SLA targets. We'll also include runbooks tailored to Dedicated.
07:24 Lisa: Regarding audit logs, do logs contain model inputs? That's sensitive. We need options to redact or only store hashes.
07:33 Priya: We can redact inputs and store metadata/hashes. Full inputs can be stored optionally with customer-managed encryption keys. We'll outline the config.
07:46 Jordan: Quick check — any blockers today that would stop us from scheduling the dry-run next week?
07:52 Tom: We need the network diagram and CIDR ranges, otherwise we're blocked.
07:56 Jordan: Noted — Tom will send those.
07:59 Tom: I'll send them by EOD tomorrow.
08:03 Maya: Also we want a 1:1 with the SE during the dry-run.
08:06 Priya: I'll be on the dry-run.
08:09 Jordan: Good.
08:12 (pause)
08:20 Priya: I'll call out one tricky item — quantized models can sometimes change generation patterns. For high-precision customer responses, we'll run quality checks and regen tests. We'll tie regressions to prompt-level evals.
08:34 Maya: Good. We'll share a gold set of prompts for eval.
08:38 Jordan: On the topic of tooling, Redwood Console will show token-level costs and tracing — does Kestrel want long-term retention for traces?
08:47 Maya: For now 30 days is fine, but we'll decide after pilot.
08:51 Priya: Okay I'll set default to 30 and note option for extended retention as an add-on.
08:57 Lisa: One more security detail — does Redwood support customer-managed certificate rotation for endpoints?
09:03 Priya: Yes, for Dedicated we can provision with customer certs or use Redwood-managed certs. We'll document rotation cadence.
09:12 Amit: For the pilot success criteria, what should we measure?
09:15 Jordan: Success criteria we discussed: p95 latency under X (we'll confirm number after baseline), cost per 1k tokens within budget, zero P0 incidents during pilot, and model output quality measured by your gold prompt evals.
09:29 Maya: Can you write those into the runbook as the pilot success section?
09:33 Priya: Will do.
09:35 (short silence)
09:42 Jordan: Any competitor intel we should be aware of? Maya?
09:45 Maya: We're also evaluating Anthropic and considering a self-hosted option for some workloads. Procurement asked to see pricing and SOC2 artifacts.
09:54 Jordan: We'll provide pricing and SOC docs.
09:58 Priya: For the technical dry-run, I'll need SSH access to an orchestrator node and a small test VPC with a peering connection to run traffic.
10:08 Tom: We'll provision a test subnet and temporary credentials.
10:12 Priya: Great. I'll also bring a small test harness that mimics your multi-turn patterns and embeddings pipeline — it's in the shared spreadsheet.
10:23 Maya: About the shared artifacts — can you drop the runbook link in the notes and the benchmark spreadsheet?
10:28 Jordan: Yep, I'll paste links after the call. For reference: runbook doc: https://redwood.app/r/runbooks/kestrel-implementation (shared, view-only)
10:38 Jordan: Benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/sheets/kestrel-benchmarks (edit for Priya)
10:46 Jordan: Security pack: https://redwood.app/sec/kestrel-package (download)
10:53 Maya: Great, thanks.
10:56 Tom: Quick question — in case we need to pin to eu-west for EU customers, is there any cost delta or delay?
11:03 Jordan: Slight cost delta for reserved capacity in region and setup lead time maybe a week to provision. We'll call out timings in the pricing template.
11:14 Lisa: Procurement will ask about data export controls and revocation. We need explicit steps to purge data upon contract end.
11:22 Priya: We'll list purge steps in the runbook and include API calls for purge plus verification hashes.
11:29 Maya: Any other items?
11:31 Amit: One ask — if we opt for on-prem later, can the same rollout policies carry over?
11:36 Priya: Mostly yes. The API surface is largely the same; you'll manage networking differently but we support a consistent config model so rollouts and canaries map across.
11:47 Jordan: Ok, wrap-up. Action recap: Priya runs perf; Jordan sends runbook and pricing; Tom shares network diagram; Lisa lists compliance items. We'll schedule dry-run for 12/19.
11:58 Maya: Sounds good, thank you.
12:01 Jordan: Thanks everyone — meeting adjourned.

Notes about transcript quality: Auto-transcription had a few mis-heard technical terms (KV cache as K-V cash, minor speaker swaps). Links and artifacts were shared post-call.
